flags.name: --help
flags.description: show this help message and exit

flags.name: --file
flags.description: File to backdoor

flags.name: --shell
flags.description: Payloads that are available for use. Use 'show' to see payloads.

flags.name: --hostip
flags.description: IP of the C2 for reverse connections.

flags.name: --port
flags.description: The port to either connect back to for reverse shells or to listen on for bind shells

flags.name: --cave_jumping
flags.description: Select this options if you want to use code cave jumping to further hide your shellcode in the binary.

flags.name: --add_new_section
flags.description: Mandating that a new section be added to the exe (better success) but less av avoidance

flags.name: --user_shellcode
flags.description: User supplied shellcode, make sure that it matches the architecture that you are targeting.

flags.name: --cave
flags.description: The cave flag will find code caves that can be used for stashing shellcode. This will print to all the code caves of a specific size.The -l flag can be use with this setting.

flags.name: --shell_length
flags.description: For use with -c to help find code caves of different sizes

flags.name: --output-file
flags.description: The backdoor output file

flags.name: --section
flags.description: New section name must be less than seven characters

flags.name: --directory
flags.description: This is the location of the files that you want to backdoor. You can make a directory of file backdooring faster by forcing the attaching of a codecave to the exe by using the -a setting.

flags.name: --change_access
flags.description: This flag changes the section that houses the codecave to RWE. Sometimes this is necessary. Enabled by default. If disabled, the backdoor may fail.

flags.name: --injector
flags.description: This command turns the backdoor factory in a hunt and shellcode inject type of mechanism. Edit the target settings in the injector module.

flags.name: --suffix
flags.description: For use with injector, places a suffix on the original file for easy recovery

flags.name: --delete_original
flags.description: For use with injector module. This command deletes the original file. Not for use in production systems. *Author not responsible for stupid uses.*

flags.name: --disk_offset
flags.description: Starting point on disk offset, in bytes. Some authors want to obfuscate their on disk offset to avoid reverse engineering, if you find one of those files use this flag, after you find the offset.

flags.name: --support_check
flags.description: To determine if the file is supported by BDF prior to backdooring the file. For use by itself or with verbose. This check happens automatically if the backdooring is attempted.

flags.name: --cave-miner
flags.description: Future use, to help determine smallest shellcode possible in a PE file

flags.name: --no_banner
flags.description: Kills the banner.

flags.name: --verbose
flags.description: For debug information output.

flags.name: --image-type
flags.description: ALL, x86, or x64 type binaries only. Default=ALL

flags.name: --zero_cert
flags.description: Allows for the overwriting of the pointer to the PE certificate table effectively removing the certificate from the binary for all intents and purposes.

flags.name: --runas_admin
flags.description: EXPERIMENTAL Checks the PE binaries for 'requestedExecutionLevel level="highestAvailable"'. If this string is included in the binary, it must run as system/admin. If not in Support Check mode it will attmept to patch highestAvailable into the manifest if requestedExecutionLevel entry exists.

flags.name: --patch_dll
flags.description: Use this setting if you DON'T want to patch DLLs. Patches by default.

flags.name: --fat_priority
flags.description: For MACH-O format. If fat file, focus on which arch to patch. Default is x64. To force x86 use -F x86, to force both archs use -F ALL.

flags.name: --beacon
flags.description: For payloads that have the ability to beacon out, set the time in secs

flags.name: --patch-method
flags.description: Patching methods for PE files, 'manual','automatic', replace and onionduke

flags.name: --user_malware
flags.description: For onionduke. Provide your desired binary.

flags.name: --xp_mode
flags.description: Default: DO NOT support for XP legacy machines, use -X to support XP. By default the binary will crash on XP machines (e.g. sandboxes)

flags.name: --idt_in_cave
flags.description: EXPERIMENTAL By default a new Import Directory Table is created in a new section, by calling this flag it will be put in a code cave. This can cause bianry failure is some cases. Test on target binaries first.

flags.name: --code_sign
flags.description: For those with codesigning certs wishing to sign PE binaries only. Name your signing key and private key signingcert.cer and signingPrivateKey.pem repectively in the certs directory it's up to you to obtain signing certs.

flags.name: --preprocess
flags.description: To execute preprocessing scripts in the preprocess directory
